open_points.subject: Randomly minted entity identifiers
open_points.text: `trial_execution_id` M07, `binding_id` M11, `run_id` M19, `approval_id` M24 and `grant_id` M25 are minted at random by the kernel; one that already exists is minted again.
open_points.question: Which module owns random identifier generation, collision detection and retry for these five record types?
options: Each record-owning module mints its own identifiers and asks `store` about collisions
A separate lower-level identifier capability owns the mechanism
open_points.default_guess: Have `store` mint and collision-check each identifier inside the record-creation transaction.

open_points.subject: Equal content submission semantics
open_points.text: `canonical_values` owns “A01 rules 1 and 4” but “Must not own Where a value is stored”; A01 rule 4 requires that existing records be returned unchanged, preserve their first author and time, and not become “the one issued last”.
open_points.question: Does `canonical_values` own only identity calculation, or does it also own the persistence-dependent equal-submission behavior; if only identity calculation, which domain module or `store` owns that behavior?
options: Each domain module owns equal-submission behavior using identities from `canonical_values`
`store` owns a generic atomic return-existing-or-insert operation
`canonical_values` owns the whole rule and therefore gains record lookup dependencies
open_points.default_guess: Limit `canonical_values` to identity calculation and make each domain module enforce equal-submission semantics through an atomic store capability.

open_points.subject: SpooledFile M22 creation
open_points.text: “Two have several, on purpose: StoredValue M21 ...; NodeExecution M23 ...” conflicts with “The module that writes a StoredValue M21 or a SpooledFile M22 sets its class” and the assignments of function files to `runs` and service files to `effects`.
open_points.question: Who owns creation of SpooledFile records: `store`, both `runs` and `effects`, or one higher module?
options: `runs` and `effects` are intentional co-owners and `store.spool_file` only persists their records
`store` is the sole SpooledFile writer and callers supply classification facts
One domain module owns every SpooledFile creation
open_points.default_guess: Treat `runs` and `effects` as intentional co-owners of SpooledFile creation, both writing through `store.spool_file`, and list M22 among the explicit multi-writer records.
